clue.text: Psychiatrist to cure the conceit of success?

definitions.text: Psychiatrist to cure the conceit of success?

parts.words: Psychiatrist to cure the conceit of success?
parts.note: a slang word for a psychiatrist read literally: success swells the head, and this person would reduce it again

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a psychiatrist can cure the vanity that success brings.
explanation.walkthrough: A swollen head is conceit; the slang name for a psychiatrist pictures someone who shrinks it back to size.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a psychiatrist, from the idea of reducing a patient's swollen ego.

clue.text: Stew made to a rich recipe .

indicators.note: a recipe mixes ingredients, so these letters are combined into a new order

explanation.surface: A stew cooked according to a luxurious recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recipe' turns the letters of TO A RICH into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Haricot mutton is a traditional French ragout, so the word names a kind of meat stew.

clue.text: Loss of speech made by Sir Alan on the Continent

parts.note: Sir Alan Herbert, the humorist A. P. Herbert, signed his pieces with his initials APH
Asia is a continent

explanation.surface: A loss of speech suffered by some knight called Alan while travelling in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Continent' suggests mainland Europe to a British reader, but here it is simply a continent, Asia. A. P. Herbert was a British writer and MP whose initials were familiar from Punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical term for the inability to produce or understand language, typically after brain damage.

clue.text: Film extra? No, Virginia is a star of rare brilliance

parts.note: a supernumerary or extra in a film is called a super
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Virginia was no mere film extra but a star of exceptional brilliance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures an actress called Virginia; 'star' is literal, an astronomical one.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploding star that briefly becomes enormously bright, so it is a star of rare brilliance.

clue.text: Progressive Hogarthian has daughter inclined to be backward

parts.note: Hogarth painted the series A Rake's Progress, so his progressing figure is the rake

explanation.surface: A forward-thinking follower of Hogarth has a daughter who tends to hang back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Progressive' seems to mean forward-thinking, but it points to Hogarth's eight paintings of a young wastrel's decline. 'backward' means sloping back, as a raked stage slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: A raked stage or mast slopes, tilting toward the back.

clue.text: It serves you right!

parts.note: reads as the taunt to someone who got what they deserved, and as the Greek goddess of retribution who deals out exactly that

explanation.surface: A gloating cry at someone who has got their comeuppance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of retribution, and so any agent of deserved downfall.

clue.text: Where Josiah went to pot-somewhere in old Italy

definitions.meaning: Josiah Wedgwood named his pottery works near Stoke-on-Trent after the ancient region
the ancient land of the Etruscans in central Italy

explanation.surface: Where Josiah went to ruin, a place somewhere in ancient Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went to pot' sounds like ruin but means making pots: Wedgwood was the famous English potter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the Wedgwood factory village in Staffordshire and the ancient Etruscan region share the name.

clue.text: The P.M.'s a crafty fellow!

parts.note: a Prime Minister forms the ministerial team, and a craftsman builds fine wooden furniture: one compound title covers both

explanation.surface: A remark that the Prime Minister is a sly character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crafty' seems to mean cunning but means skilled at a craft. P.M. is Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who builds fine furniture, and punningly a premier who forms the government.

clue.text: Dries off joint in flying-machine

parts.note: to air washing is to dry it off
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: Someone dries a cut of meat in some flying contraption.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirigible is a powered lighter-than-air craft, an early flying-machine.

clue.text: German communist admits defeat?

definitions.meaning: the German word for comrade, as communists address each other
the cry German soldiers shouted when surrendering

explanation.surface: A German communist concedes that he has lost.
explanation.walkthrough: In the First World War, German troops surrendering called out this word, meaning comrade.
explanation.definitionFit: Comrade in German, and the word called out by German soldiers giving themselves up.

clue.text: The Darwinian issue was a paternal inheritance

definitions.meaning: something handed down through the male line

explanation.surface: Darwin's offspring was something inherited from the father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' means a published book, not children.
explanation.definitionFit: Title of Darwin's book on human evolution, and literally lineage passed from father to son.

clue.text: Part of da Vinci's original idea for a food-cutter

indicators.note: the answer is only a portion of these words, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Part of Leonardo's original design for a machine to slice food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' points into 'Vinci's original', where the answer runs across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A front tooth with a sharp edge for biting, so it cuts food.

clue.text: They are due to rats!

parts.note: rats get their just rewards, and rats are said to abandon a sinking ship: both senses of one word

explanation.surface: An exclamation that rats will get what they have coming.
explanation.definitionFit: What one deserves, as in just deserts, and also abandons, as rats leave a sinking ship.

clue.text: Run out of half-tracks

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, as in ex-directory

indicators.note: half of the six-letter word is taken, its first three letters

explanation.surface: Leaving a set of half-track military vehicles behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-tracks' reads as the vehicle, but 'half' takes TRA from 'tracks'. 'Run' is the cricket sense: a run not scored off the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bye or wide is a run added to the score but not hit by the batter.

clue.text: A different sort of case, but obscure

indicators.note: a different sort of these letters means arranging them in another order

explanation.surface: A rather different case, but a puzzling one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A different sort' rearranges OF CASE BUT; 'obscure' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To obfuscate is to make unclear, the same as to obscure something.

clue.text: Popular measure, in step with tradition

parts.note: folk means of the people, popular
a measure is an old word for a stately dance

explanation.surface: A popular measure that keeps pace with established custom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'measure' looks like a quantity but is the old word for a dance; the definition pictures dancing steps handed down by tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional dance of a people, whose steps are passed down through generations.

clue.text: Champion's success here in days of Empire

definitions.text: Champion's success here in days of Empire

parts.words: Champion's success here in days of Empire
parts.note: Harry Champion was a Victorian and Edwardian comic singer whose fame was won on the variety stage

explanation.surface: Where a sporting champion triumphed in imperial times.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Champion was a popular British variety singer around 1900; the surface reads 'Champion' as a sporting winner.
explanation.definitionFit: The popular variety theatre of Victorian and Edwardian Britain, the stage where Harry Champion made his name.

clue.text: Superficial judge of Shakespeare

definitions.meaning: Justice ... is a country magistrate in Henry IV Part 2 and The Merry Wives of Windsor

explanation.surface: A superficial critic of Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'judge of' seems to mean a critic, but it is a justice who appears in Shakespeare's plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking depth, and the name of a foolish country magistrate in two Shakespeare plays.

clue.text: Statement of legal authority giving entitlement to an article

definitions.meaning: in law, the heading of a document stating where, when and by what authority it was made
a heading or title given to a newspaper article or picture

explanation.surface: A statement of legal power granting someone the right to an item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entitlement' seems to mean a right, but it means giving a title, a heading.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a legal heading showing a document's authority and the headline over an article.

clue.text: Scope for a doctor with sex-appeal?

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
it is old slang for sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: Is there room for a doctor with sex appeal?
explanation.definitionFit: Range or extent, the scope of something.

clue.text: A top-class composer goes to eastern inn

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: A first-rate composer travels to an inn in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A French word for a country inn, used in English too.

clue.text: Army commander associated with a freebooter

parts.note: brig is short for brigadier, an army officer commanding a brigade
and joins one thing with another

explanation.surface: An army officer allied with a pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit or outlaw, just as a freebooter is a plundering adventurer.

clue.text: Stone-worker sleeping soundly?

definitions.meaning: a craftsman who shapes flints by striking them
one who is napping, with the silent first letter making the word sound the same

explanation.surface: A stonemason sleeps deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' seems to mean deeply but is a sound hint: with the K silent the word is said like napper, one who naps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flint-knapper chips stone into tools, and the spoken word matches someone taking a nap.

clue.text: Just claim to title

definitions.meaning: an entitlement, as in a ... to property

explanation.surface: Simply a claim to an inheritance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'merely' but is the adjective fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Means both morally correct and a legal entitlement to something.

clue.text: Make notes and put short question about operation

parts.note: D and E are musical notes
brief means short

explanation.surface: Take notes and ask a brief question about an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make notes' suggests writing, but D and E are two musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: To interrogate someone after a mission to gather information about how it went.

clue.text: The stock of brass the fool lost

annotationWithheld.why: The stock of brass the fool lost (7): 'The stock' (rolling stock) and 'of brass' (rich, rolling in money) fit, but no reading accounts for 'the fool lost'
annotationWithheld.clue: The stock of brass the fool lost

clue.text: Non-existent goal of eastern religion?

parts.note: the Buddhist goal is extinction of self, a state of non-existence, so the goal is literally non-existent

explanation.surface: A sceptic suggests the aim of an eastern faith does not really exist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Buddhist state of release in which desire and individual self are extinguished.

clue.text: How to start sounding like a shirker

definitions.text: How to start sounding like a shirker

parts.words: How to start sounding like a shirker
parts.note: a sailor measures depth by casting a weighted line, and the same phrase is slang for idling on the job

explanation.surface: Advice on how to begin talking like a slacker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' seems to mean speaking but means measuring water depth with a weighted line.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for shirking duty, originally the sailor's job of casting a weighted line to measure depth.
